prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The API now requires `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and checks roles. A missing or unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized`, and a known key without permission gets 403 `forbidden`. Every request other than a GET is written to the audit log with its status, including refused ones (key name is null when no known key was sent), and `GET /audit` lists the entries newest first for managers only. `npm test` (30 tests) and `npm run lint` pass. Things to know: (1) The data now has two new collections, so I raised the schema to version 3 and added a migration from version 2. Because of that I also updated the CLI test, which expects "schema 1 → 3". (2) `data/db.json` is unchanged. It upgrades when opened but has no keys, so a server running on it rejects every request until you add a manager key to the file. (3) The keys in `data/seed.json` (`dev-viewer-key`, `dev-cook-key`, `dev-manager-key`) are for development only. (4) Cooks can enter stock-take counts but cannot start or finish a stock-take; managers do that. (5) Existing tests send the manager key through the test helper, and I added `tests/auth.test.js`.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
